record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Given a colored graph representing a closed PL n-manifold M, derive purely combinatorial descriptions of the higher homotopy groups pi_i(M) for all i >= 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An (n+1)-edge-colored graph is a pair (G, γ) where G is a finite multigraph (without loops) that is regular of degree n+1, and γ : E(G) → {0, 1, …, n} is an edge-coloring such that any two edges sharing a vertex receive distinct colors. To such a colored graph one associates an n-dimensional pseudocomplex K(G) as follows: take one n-simplex σ(v) for each vertex v of G, label the vertices of each σ(v) by the colors 0, 1, …, n, and glue σ(v) to σ(w) along their (n−1)-faces opposite the vertex labeled c whenever v and w are joined in G by an edge of color c. The colored graph (G, γ) is said to represent a closed PL n-manifold M if K(G) is piecewise-linearly homeomorphic to M; equivalently, for every choice of n colors, each connected component of the subgraph spanned by the edges of those n colors represents the standard PL (n−1)-sphere.

Problem. Develop, for every integer i ≥ 2, a purely combinatorial description (a procedure depending only on the colored graph data (G, γ)) of the i-th homotopy group π_i(M) of the closed PL n-manifold M represented by (G, γ). That is, give a combinatorial algorithm or formula that takes (G, γ) as input and outputs a presentation of π_i(M) for each i ≥ 2.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard surveys and recent papers on crystallization / gem theory describe combinatorial computations of homology, fundamental group, and various PL invariants from colored graphs, but no combinatorial description of the higher homotopy groups π_i (i ≥ 2) of the represented manifold appears in the literature; the question is generally regarded as an open problem in the gem-theoretic program.

status_evidence.title: Manifold crystallization - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Crystallizations provide a combinatorial representation of closed PL manifolds; classical invariants like fundamental group and homology can be read off, but higher homotopy descriptions are not given.
status_evidence.claim: Standard combinatorial outputs from crystallizations cover π_1 and homology, not π_i for i ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: Kirby diagrams, trisections and gems of PL 4-manifolds: relationships, results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: A recent survey of gem-theoretic results and open problems for PL 4-manifolds, discussing combinatorial invariants but not providing combinatorial higher homotopy groups.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys list combinatorial invariants from gems but do not provide combinatorial higher homotopy groups.

status_evidence.title: A graph-theoretical representation of PL-manifolds — A survey on crystallizations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of crystallization theory describing graph-theoretical computation of fundamental group and homology of represented PL manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys describe combinatorial computation only of low-dimensional invariants of M.
